app.footer: Pantheon Typology. A first version, not yet tested on a large sample.

epigraph.text: All things are full of gods.

intro.modelTitle: Seven questions, two gods to each
intro.modelIntro: Each line on the wheel is a question with a god at either end. Nobody is all one god. The test places you on all seven lines, then names the god you lean to hardest and the one facing it across the wheel, whom you have probably been neglecting.
intro.headline: Find the god you lead with, and the one you neglect.
intro.lede: The Greeks had a god for most ways of being a person. This test sets fourteen of them against each other in pairs. You rate {count} statements, and it tells you which god of each pair you take after.
intro.wheelCaption: Each line joins two gods who want opposite things.

facts.detail: Your answers are never sent anywhere.
Not yet tested on a large sample. Treat the result as a sketch.

quiz.instruction: Compared with most people you know, how true is each statement of you?
quiz.scaleHelp: Left is far less true of you than of most people you know. Right is far more. The middle circle means about the same.
quiz.missingOne: One statement on this page has no answer yet.
quiz.missingMany: {n} statements on this page have no answer yet.

result.neglectedRule: The Greeks held that every god is owed something, and that the one to fear is the one you leave out. Hippolytus gave everything to Artemis and would not so much as greet Aphrodite. Euripides wrote the play about how that went.
result.wheelIntro: Seven dots, one on every line. The further a dot sits from the centre, the stronger the pull toward the god at that end. A hollow dot at the centre is a line with no pull either way.
result.wheelStrongest: The ringed dot is your strongest pull: {god}.
result.wheelStill: All seven dots sit at the centre. No god has any pull on you.
result.wheelSpoken: Your seven dots on the wheel. {reading}
result.polaritiesIntro: The longer the bar, the stronger the pull toward the god on that side.
result.balancedNote: Balanced. Neither god has much of a hold here.
result.retakeConfirm: Clear my answers and start again
result.copy: Copy a link to this result
result.sharedNotice: This result was opened from a link. Your own answers are untouched.
result.incomplete: There is no result until every statement has an answer.

gods.title: The fourteen gods
gods.intro: Seven pairs of opposites. In each cloud of words, the larger a word is set, the more it belongs to the god.

credits.title: The plates
credits.intro: Every statue and painting on this site, with the collection that holds it, where the photograph came from and its licence. The statues are shown in black and white, and all the pictures are cropped.
